# Preface {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note}
## About this adaptation
This book is an adaptation of Rafael A. Irizarry's *Introduction to Data Science* (<https://rafalab.github.io/dsbook-part-1/>), created by Giorgio Arcara for the *Behavioural Data Science* course (PS0000002, University of Padua). Substantive changes — replaced datasets and case studies, new chapters, retitling — are documented in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/intro-to-behds/behdsbook-part-1/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

This work remains licensed under [CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0), consistent with the original.
:::

This is the website for the **Data Wrangling and Visualization with R** part of **Introduction to Behavioural Data Science**, an adaptation of **Introduction to Data Science**.

This behavioural-science adaptation, *Introduction to Behavioural Data Science*, was created by Giorgio Arcara for the *Behavioural Data Science* course (PS0000002, University of Padua).

The Quarto files used to generate this adaptation are available on [GitHub](https://github.com/intro-to-behds/behdsbook-part-1)[^index-8].

[^index-8]: <https://github.com/intro-to-behds/behdsbook-part-1>

The website for the original book are the following:

- Part 1 **Data Wrangling and Visualization with R** part is [here](http://rafalab.dfci.harvard.edu/dsbook-part-1/)[^index-1].
- Part 2 **Statistics and Prediction Algorithms Through Case Studies** part is [here](http://rafalab.dfci.harvard.edu/dsbook-part-2/)[^index-2].

[^index-1]: <http://rafalab.dfci.harvard.edu/dsbook-part-1/>
[^index-2]: <http://rafalab.dfci.harvard.edu/dsbook-part-2/>


# Disclaimers

In this version of the book, all examples and datasets are adaptations of the datasets in the original book, re-themed to fit a behavioural-science context. The numerical values derive from real datasets, but their behavioural framing is fictional: **these should not be interpreted or cited as genuine behavioural data**.

The English translation and adaptation were produced with the assistance of _Claude Code (Sonnet 4.6)_. The model was used for programming and language revision only; it did not generate new content or ideas.

# Acknowledgments to the Original Edition {.unnumbered}

*The following are Rafael A. Irizarry's original acknowledgments, unchanged.*

This book is dedicated to all the people involved in building and maintaining R and the R packages we use in this book. A special thanks to the developers and maintainers of base R, the tidyverse, data.table, and the caret package.

A special thanks to Jenna Landy for her careful editing and helpful advice on this book; to David Robinson for generously answering many questions about the tidyverse and aiding in my understanding of it; and to Amy Gill for dozens of comments, edits, and suggestions. Also, many thanks to Stephanie Hicks who twice served as a co-instructor in my data science classes and Yihui Xie who patiently put up with my many questions related to markdown. Thanks also to Karl Broman, from whom I borrowed ideas for the Data Visualization and Productivity Tools parts. Thanks to Peter Aldhous from whom I borrowed ideas for the principles of data visualization section and Jenny Bryan for writing *Happy Git and GitHub for the useR*, which influenced our Git chapters. Also, many thanks to Jeff Leek, Roger Peng, and Brian Caffo, whose onlile classes inspired the way this book is divided, to Garrett Grolemund and Hadley Wickham for making the markdown code for their R for Data Science book open, and the editors, John Kimmel and Lara Spieker, for their support. Finally, thanks to Alex Nones for proofreading the manuscript during its various stages.

This book was conceived during the teaching of several applied statistics courses, starting over fifteen years ago. The teaching assistants working with me throughout the years made important indirect contributions to this book. The material was further refined during a HarvardX series coordinated by Heather Sternshein and Zofia Gajdos. We thank them for their contributions. We are also grateful to all the students whose questions and comments helped us improve the book. The courses were partially funded by NIH grant R25GM114818. We are very grateful to the National Institutes of Health for its support.
